summary: An Amstrad CPC cracktro by Tristar and Red Sector Inc., coded, drawn and scored by Raft, which placed third in the Intro compo at @Party 2015.
why: A one-person production that placed in a party compo, done in the classic trainer-menu style with options, credits and greetings.

summary: An Atari 8-bit invitation to Silly Venture 2016 by Mystic Bytes, F#READY and Lamers, which placed 2nd in the Realtime Wild compo at Outline 2016. A big party logo sits under a cyclist riding across a desert strip while a scroller gives the details.
why: A party invitation that took second place in Outline 2016's Realtime Wild compo, with code by Wieczor and F#READY and graphics from mOOnie, Odyn1ec and Wieczor.

summary: A ZX Spectrum 48K demo by Speccy.pl, coded by Tygrys with AY music by V0yager and graphics by CatMan and Piesiu. It placed third in the Oldschool Demo compo at Riverwash 2015.
why: A third place at Riverwash 2015 from the Polish Speccy.pl crew, and it runs on a stock 48K Spectrum.

summary: EXclusive ON's 16K C64 intro, coded and scored by Jammer with a charset logo by Joe, which won the Intro Creation Competition 2018: a big 3D-looking EXON logo over a bouncing, tilted-letter scroller.
why: Sceners single out the scroller, with each letter tilted as if it had bounced into place, plus the speed-up and slow-down of the scroll, the catchy tune and how tightly it all syncs.

quote.text: the tilting of the charset is especially cool as it gives the impression the letters just bounced there randomly. Also the speedup/slowdown of the scroll is perfect.

summary: A C64 4K intro by Plush, with code by Krill, graphics by Caprice and music by Fanta, that won the C64 4K intro compo at Mekka & Symposium 2000.
why: A compo winner that sceners still rate highly. They single out its clean, clear look and its lined effects, which Krill says were inspired by an earlier release.

quote.text: One of the top productions in the past, looking just as clean and clear today. I always liked those lined effects

summary: Oxyron's demo for the Commodore 64 DTV, the joystick-sized C64 clone, which placed joint second in the Oldschool Demo compo at Nordlicht 2018. Code by Axis and Peiselulli, music by dEViLOCk, graphics by Yazoo.
why: A rare chance to see what the DTV can do. Sceners praise how smooth it all runs and single out the rotating triangle tunnel, and some felt it deserved the win.

quote.text: i'm not familiar with DTV specs but all looks so smooth to me, o'som gfx and speed together with sid vibes makes me smile.

summary: Oxyron's New Year 8K intro for the C64, coded by Axis with graphics by Yazoo and music by Linus. It won the 8K Intro Competition 2017 and greets 2018 with a crossed layout of horizontal and vertical scrolling parts.
why: Sceners point to the screen set-up of horizontal and vertical parts and the antialiased vector, and to how much was fitted into 8K. It took first place in its compo.

quote.text: Nice what you put into 8k!! One of my favourites in the compo!

summary: Noice's first demo for the Commodore 64-DTV (the DTV2/Hummer), a short one-filer released in May 2007 and recorded off a TV screen by its author.
why: An early demo made for the C64-DTV hardware. Sceners called it nice for first DTV work and said it showed the machine's potential, though some found it short.

quote.text: shows the potential of the dtv

summary: Desire's Atari XL/XE demo, placing second in the Atari XL/XE Demo compo at Silly Venture 2k24 WE. The video title calls it a 12k intro, built around flat-shaded 3D scenes.
why: A runner-up at Silly Venture, the main Atari 8-bit party, with a dedicated 3D engine by Probe and 3D scenes designed by Heaven.

summary: Benediction's 32K intro for the Amstrad CPC, with code and text by Eliot, graphics by Voxfreax and music by Dma-Sc. It won the combined demo/intro compo at Benediction Coding Party #3 in 2023.
why: A compo winner at Benediction's own coding party, and a compact 32K showcase from a long-running CPC group.

summary: Simon Quernhorst's Atari VCS demo, with music by Manuel Polik and design help from Falk Heinzelmann, placed 6th in the Console/Real Wild compo at Breakpoint 2008.
why: A rare demo for the Atari 2600, a machine with very little to work with, shown in a mixed console and wild compo at Breakpoint.

summary: A one-file demo by Oxyron for the Commodore 64 DTV: a field of 3068 sine-plotted dots swirls above Yazoo's colourful Oxyron logo while a scroller runs between them.
why: One of the few DTV demos of its time. Sceners praised the fast blitter-driven plotting routine, the logo using more than 16 colours and the music, which manages without the SID filters the DTV lacks.

quote.text: Most beautiful sineplots ever! Stylish logo too!

summary: An invitation intro for Amstrad CPC by Pulpo Corrosivo and Futurs', with code by Toms, music by Zik on a patched player and graphics by Beb.
why: A joint invitation from two groups, released with little else on record. The fact sheet notes no compo entry or awards, so it stands as a short party invitro for CPC followers.

summary: The Graphic Demo is a 1986 Atari 8-bit demo pack from Compy-Shop, with code, graphics and music by Peter Sabath and additional graphics by Frogdesign.
why: An early Atari 8-bit demo from the mid-eighties, made largely by one person, and a look at what the machine's commercial software scene was showing off at the time.
highlights: Compy Shop logo over colour bars

summary: Gasman's ZX Spectrum demo, released at Sundown 2014 where it took second place in the Old School Demo competition. The video is a camera recording of the big-screen showing at the party.
why: A podium finish at Sundown 2014 in the Old School Demo compo, and it runs on a stock 48K Spectrum with AY music.

summary: An Amstrad CPC demo by Overlanders from 2009, coded by Candy with a logo by Beb, font by Barjack and music by Tom&Jerry. A tomato logo sits beside a framed window of greetings text over a moving pattern.
why: No placings or comments to go on, but it's a compact single-screen Overlanders production with a full credit line of code, graphics and music.

summary: wAMMA's Atari 2600 demo, coded by visy, Ilmarque and tatu, which placed 4th in the combined demo compo at Simulaatio 2007.
why: A scene demo on the VCS, one of the most cramped machines there is, with tatu credited separately for raster effects and Ilmarque handling the music as well as code and graphics.

summary: TSJ's tongue-in-cheek C64 demo that won the C64 demo compo at Fioniadata 2026, with code by Trap, graphics by The Sarge and music by Jammer.
why: Sceners singled out Jammer's soundtrack above all, along with The Sarge's pixels and the cheeky humour. Several call it entertaining and well made despite, or because of, its daft theme.

quote.text: I dig. I hate picking up anyone with such a hard core lineup, but I'm going to do it anyway... that track by Jammer, oh my.

summary: Fairlight's short C64 demo from Big Floppy People 2007, where it came third in the C64 demo compo. Code and graphics by Hollowman and Oxidy, music by Fegolhuzz.
why: Sceners single out Fegolhuzz's tune and the lava-lamp test tube, and like its style despite finding it too short. Some at the party preferred it to the two demos placed above it.

quote.text: Cool style and really neat lavalamp/test tube/alien blood cocktail.

summary: Smash Designs' C64 demo, coded and drawn by AEG with music by SoNiC, which took third in the C64 demo compo at Mekka & Symposium 2001.
why: Sceners single out its Doom-style raycaster part, praised for running in 16 colours, along with SoNiC's soundtrack. Some note it recycles less than other Triage releases, though others find its zoomers and rotators rough.

quote.text: the doom part is still unmatched with its 16 colors.... coders anyone ? :)

summary: Extend's two-disk-side C64 demo that won the demo compo at Zoo 2026, mixing hand-coded effects with new animation players built over two years.
why: Sceners praise its distinctive, forward-looking style, pacing and a soundtrack that evolves as essentially one track through the demo; several compare its vibe to early Orange PC demos.

quote.text: Far beyond the usual wankery of being able to place one more sprite on the screen compared to the previous record holder and yet it's also technically impressive.

summary: A 2K intro for the Atari VCS, coded by SvOlli with music by SunSpire, which won the Oldschool Demo compo at Deadline 2017.
why: It took first place in Deadline 2017's Oldschool Demo compo, beating full-size entries with a 2K Atari 2600 cartridge.

summary: Reflex's ninth C64 demo, which won the C64 demo compo at The Party 1996. Code by Zorc and Adder, music by Jeff and Praiser, and pictures from Earthquake, Felidae, Amoeba and Warp 8.
why: Sceners remember it as a strong showing after several big names had left the C64, with effects new to the machine at the time: landscape, blobs, a fractal colour zoomer, a chessboard flight and rotozoomers. The ski animation drew cheers in the hall.

quote.text: For its time, it had quite some revolutionary effects on C64 such as landscape, blob potentials, fractal colorzoomer, flight through chessboards and many rotzoomers.

summary: An Amstrad CPC demo coded by Jack with music by Mad Max, released at the RTS 1998 party, where it won the OldSkool Demos on pre-1990 machines compo.
why: It took first place in the old-school demo compo at RTS 1998, the party it is named after, so it's a good look at the CPC scene's late-1990s work.

summary: Samar Productions and EXclusive ON's C64 tribute to The Prodigy's Keith Flint, second in the C64 demo compo at Forever 2019: a large portrait, a lower-border sprite scroller and Jammer's cover of Voodoo People.
why: Sceners single out Jammer's cover, built without samples on a 50Hz tune, along with the artwork and scrolltext. Most of the code was put together in a single day at the party.

quote.text: The music, the artwork, the scrolltext. A perfect tribute for a heartfelt loss.

summary: A ZX Spectrum demo by Thesuper that won the Combined 8-Bit Demo compo at DiHalt 2015.
why: It took first place in DiHalt 2015's combined 8-bit demo competition, beating entries from other 8-bit machines.

summary: Hack n' Trade's PETSCII demo for the Commodore 64, placed 7th in the C64 demo compo at Datastorm 2014. Graphics by acidT*rroreast, music by Goto80, code by Mathman, running as an endless loop.
why: Sceners praise the tight sync between Goto80's music and the graphics, the fitting sound effects and the sense of things breaking apart, and say the PETSCII scenes reward repeat viewing.

quote.text: those PETSCII diamonds are watchable so many times, you always find something new you've missed before.

summary: An Easter intro for the Atari 8-bit by Mad Team and Agenda, released on 1 April 2013, with code by Tebe, music by stRing and graphics by Ooz.
why: A small seasonal release from two Polish-scene groups. Its main draw is the large hand-drawn picture by Ooz, paired with stRing's music.

summary: An Amstrad CPC demo by Overlanders from 2002, with code, graphics and music shared between Madram, Eliot, Epsilon and BDC Iron, and extra graphics by Beb, Fafa and Grim.
why: A group effort from several Overlanders members. Its soundtrack includes AY covers of Harold Faltermeyer's Axel F. and Jeroen Tel's C64 Eliminator tune.

summary: A ZX Spectrum 128K demo by Kpacku, released in January 2017, with code and fonts by Trefi, graphics by Tutty and music by NQE.
why: A thin fact sheet, but it is tagged for the Spectrum's multicolour mode, and the credits show a small team behind code, graphics and music.
highlights: quotes from Picasso and Da Vinci

summary: Cosine's Atari 8-bit demo, coded by TMR with music by Bex, which won the Atari Demo compo at Forever 2014. It plays out entirely in shades of grey.
why: It took first place in the Atari demo competition at Forever 2014.

summary: Dual Crew's C64 demo built around an FLI picture of Galactus, with sprite scrollers running over it. It came 2nd in the Oldskool Demo compo at Sundown 2013.
why: Sceners praised it as one of the best sprites-over-FLI parts they had seen, with the FLI bug so well hidden that it hardly looks like FLI. They also liked ne7's soundtrack.

quote.text: This is real quality shit! One of the best sprites-over-fli parts i have seen.

summary: A 1K intro for the Atari 8-bit by Taquart, coded by Eru, which came second in the Atari 1K Intro compo at Forever 2004.
why: A podium finish in a size-limited compo at Forever 2004, showing what Eru could fit into a single kilobyte on the Atari.

summary: A New Year greeting demo by Buyan and Splinter for an enhanced ZX Spectrum, released in January 2015. It won the New Year Gift compo at CC Winter / DiHalt Lite.2015.
why: It took first place in its New Year Gift compo, and is a short seasonal card from the Russian Spectrum scene.

summary: New Generation's Atari Lynx demo that won the Lynx demo compo at Silly Venture 2k20+1 SE in 2021, set to Gydra's drum and bass track "Hearing Damage".
why: A compo winner on a rarely used handheld. Solo and Laoo share the code, and Solo, Tiger and kris3d made the graphics, including 3D work.

summary: A 1K intro for the Atari 8-bit by MaPa (code) and PG (music) that won the Atari 1K compo at Forever 2015. Grey silhouettes of objects stand on a beach-like horizon, each casting a long striped shadow.
why: It won its compo at Forever 2015 and was nominated for Best Low-End intro at The Meteoriks 2016, a rare showing for a 1K Atari production.

summary: Fairlight's C64 demo that won the demo compo at Transmission64 2023, coded by Trident with music by Fegolhuzz and graphics by Pal, tNG and Soya.
why: Nominated for 8-bit demo at Siggraph Asia 2023. Sceners praise the char manipulations, the timing to the music and the activity in the borders, and marvel that Trident coded it almost alone.
highlights: scroller that moves with the beat

quote.text: Tasteful! Great code, gfx and music, all timed to perfection! Love the theme. And all the stuff going on in the borders.

summary: Cyberpunks Unity's ZX Spectrum demo, third in the 8 bit 640Kb Demo compo at Chaos Constructions 2004. A political piece in red on grey, with propaganda-style silhouettes and slogans.
why: A placing at Chaos Constructions and an unusual subject: tagged for communism, Lenin and anticapitalism, it's an openly political demo on the Spectrum.

summary: Samar Productions' two-disk-side C64 demo, the final version of the 95% release that won North Party '97, adding a clean directory and part selectors on both disk sides. Code by a large team, music by Daf and Dune.
why: Sceners single out its fast pace and the tight sync between effects and an unusual, break-heavy soundtrack; several call it Samar's best and one of their all-time favourite C64 demos.

quote.text: I'm still impressed by the great connection between the music and the effects.

summary: A 16K intro for the Atari 8-bit by g0blinish, with music by Caruso. It came second in the Atari XL/XE 16kb intro compo at Silly Venture 2k18.
why: A second place at Silly Venture in a size-limited category, and the source code is available for anyone curious how it fits in 16K.

summary: Crest's C64 demo, largely a one-man effort by Dane on code, graphics, music and text, that won the demo compo at Little Computer People 2002. It's built around X-FLI photographic portraits, with four tunes across the parts.
why: Sceners call it an insane one-man effort and single out the picture conversions and Dane's music, including his cover of Virt's "Flowerguy's Pool Party". The disks also carry extras such as the X-FLI editor and a part selector.

quote.text: Dane is not a trickster, but a full-blown C64 magician.

summary: CopperZoom is a 32-byte intro for the Atari 8-bit by SquoQuo, released in November 2012.
why: A 32-byte intro is about as small as size-limited code gets. This one is a compact example of what fits into that budget on the Atari.

summary: Gemba Boys' ZX Spectrum 128K demo, placing 2nd in the ZX Spectrum Demo compo at Forever 2019, with code by Noby, Mike, Gasman and Busy, and music and graphics by Aki and PG.
why: A runner-up at Forever 2019 from a crew pooling several well-known Spectrum coders, with an AY soundtrack made in Vortex Tracker II.

summary: Extend's C64 demo that came second in the demo compo at X 2006, with code by Barfly, Muhmi and Tape, music by Barracuda and graphics by Duce, all built around a kinky rubber-and-leather theme.
why: Sceners single out the unusual fetish theme carried through the whole demo, Barracuda's fitting soundtrack and the twisters, including a seven-colour one. Some found the graphics uneven.

quote.text: this demo rules. it has a spanking theme throughout the whole demo, which is rare. the awesome soundtrack fits very very well.

summary: Impact's Amstrad CPC demo released on Christmas Day 2023, with code and graphics by AST, further graphics by Kris and Hwikaa, and music by Tomchi.
why: A recent release from a long-running CPC group. The video title marks it as a CRTC-1 demo, written for that specific CPC display chip.

summary: Vanity's 16K intro for the Amstrad CPC, coded by Hicks with graphics by Beb and music by e-dredon. A large chunky pixel picture of an eye sits under a scrolling text message.
why: Tagged as an entry in the rotozoomer challenge, it puts a rotozoomer into a 16K CPC intro. It was released in 2025 with no compo placing listed.

summary: Mahoney's C64 demo built around subpixel rendering, with lft on music, which took third in the C64 demo compo at Datastorm 2011. A slow, storybook-paced run of hires pictures and smoothly moving text.
why: Sceners praise it for trying something new and pulling it off, and for being a calm, stylish demo that earns its standing without much bang. Many likened it to leafing through a childhood storybook.

quote.text: absolutely loved this - really reminded me of some story books I read as a child.

summary: Phonics' C64 demo, placed 4th in the demo compo at Zoo 2024 (party version): a fast-cut, glitch-styled ride with rabbit animations and bold typography, split into an A-side and a B-side like a record.
why: Sceners single out its style, pacing and design over raw code, with Flotsam's techno soundtrack, the twerking bunnies and the mixed typography drawing most praise. Many felt it deserved a higher placing.

quote.text: Funky as hell! Great animations. Love the mix of fonts which change on the screen and the fast cut scenes. Really great audio-visual aesthetics!

summary: Noice's MSX2 demo, coded by Shadow with graphics by Rocket and music by Yerzmyey, which came second in the Other Platform Demo compo at Gerp 2015.
why: A second place at Gerp 2015 against other platforms, and a recent example of a Noice production on the MSX2.
highlights: scroller text curving across the screen

summary: Proxima's demo for the original 32K BBC Micro, placing 2nd in the Oldschool Demo compo at Deadline 2021. Code by Leuat, music by mAZE and Mibri, graphics by Leuat, Optic and Hammerfist.
why: A rare modern demo for the stock BBC Micro that took second place at Deadline 2021. It is built with TRSE, Leuat's Turbo Rascal Syntax Error toolkit.
